accepted_edits.reason: The edits answer this round's content and design findings as recorded on each answer
lead ruling 2026-11-15 on existing done sections, recorded in section 4 after its node's measurement

findings.reason: the plan must name the existing closure record and renderer as what §3 extends, or its endpoint forks the record the close op already requires.
findings.text: §3 asks for `reckon evidence synthesize` to write a plan's closure overview, but that command already exists with exactly that name and job: it calls `synthesize_landed_record` (`reckon/evidence.py:810`), which reads the plan's section comments and its committed ledger runs and renders them through `_render_document` (`reckon/evidence.py:434`) into `docs/evidence/archive/<slug>-landed.html` (`_evidence_record_path`, `reckon/evidence.py:102`); the section is a redesign of an existing renderer, not a new command, and as written a worker would add a parallel command or a parallel document beside one the close op requires

findings.reason: a second closure document beside the required one duplicates the owner and leaves the required file's fragment-reading renderer untouched; `_render_document and the fragment readers are one module and one behaviour change.
findings.text: §3 says the overview "reads no fragment", but the component it would replace already reads fragments (`compose_landed_record` at `reckon/evidence.py:687`, `_fragment_body_bytes` at `reckon/evidence.py:640:759`) and a resynthesis keeps appended anchors from them (tests/test_a_resynthesis_keeps_appended_anchors.py); §3 also names no output path, so it does not say whether it replaces `docs/evidence/archive/<slug>-landed.html` — the file `_require_terminal_evidence` (`reckon/_store.py:5176`) refuses a close without — or writes a second document beside it

findings.reason: the guard must be added to that list, and the plan must reconcile its rule with the evidence-record guard that already refuses a close, or two guards will disagree about what a close owes.
findings.text: §4 proposes a close guard for a done section with no landing comment and no run record, but the close op already routes every terminal guard through one list in `validate_landing_patch` (`reckon/_store.py:5101`, called from `_apply_close` at `reckon/_store.py:4768`), which already runs `_require_every_section_ticked` (`reckon/_store.py:5010`), `_require_terminal_evidence` (`reckon/_store.py:5176`, which refuses closure without a typed evidence record) and the continuation guard; a new close check written anywhere else forks the guard list that both writers (op and merge-patch) share

findings.reason: the plan must state the check as an extension of the existing manifest auditor and path resolver, and settle the directory to the per-node convention, or the check refuses the very figures its own contract asks for.
findings.text: §2's figure check adds a new validator, but the manifest check owner already exists (`audit_manifest`, `reckon/crew/reports.py:2678`, read by `crew check --manifest`), the figure rule is already stated in the composed prompt (`reckon/crew/prompts.py:196-197`, `:233-234`, which already tell a worker to write under `docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/`), and the figure directory is already resolved by the dispatch claim owner (`_landing_fragment_paths`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:1331`, and the plan-wide topic at `:1283`); §2 states the directory as `docs/figures/<plan>/`, which disagrees with the per-node directory both the prompt and the claim resolver enforce, so a figure written where the contract says lands outside where the check looks

findings.reason: the page must be written from the sprint close owner and consume each plan's overview record rather than recompute its counts, or the sprint page and the plan overview can disagree about the same plan.
findings.text: §5 makes closing a sprint write one page, but sprint close already has an owner (`_close_sprint_with_carry_forward`, `reckon/project_state.py:2442`), and the page's per-plan counts (sections landed, runs, hours, headline result) and figure list would come from the §3 overview; re-deriving them from `ledger.runs` and a fresh `docs/figures/` walk duplicates, respectively, `reckon/evidence.py` and the figure inventory owner (`reckon/figures.py`, plus the `with_figures` ledger read at `reckon/ledger.py:3772`)

findings.reason: one section should own the landing accessor (sections × comments × runs × figures) and §2/§4/§5 consume it, which changes what those sections' done-whens assert.
findings.text: the plan's five sections each read the same relation ("a landed section has a landing comment, a run record and any figure") from raw sources on their own paths: §2 checks figures against commits, §3 renders sections from `plan.comments` and `ledger.runs`, §4 checks the same pair at close, §5 rolls the same counts up per plan; no section names a single accessor that answers "what did this section land", so the relation must be implemented four times and the four cannot be held in agreement

findings.reason: each section that widens a counted family must state in its own text what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be; here §4 and §2 add refusals and a field without either, and §3's apparent addition is really a duplicate of existing surface.
findings.text: public_definitions 2737, cli_options 488, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; §4 adds a new close refusal ("close refused: section(s) … have no landing") without naming any refusal it retires or merges, and §2 adds a manifest key plus new manifest-check findings likewise unaccounted; §3 presents `reckon evidence synthesize` as new surface when it is already present in the 488-option CLI, and names nothing it retires

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — one relation ("what a section's landing consists of") is read by four separate endpoints (manifest check, closure overview, close guard, sprint page), each re-deriving it from comments + ledger runs instead of one accessor.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 duplicates the owner of the closure document (`reckon/evidence.py`), §4 duplicates the close guard list (`reckon/_store.py`), §5 duplicates the sprint close (`reckon/project_state.py`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2737, cli_options 488, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; §2 adds a manifest key and §4 adds a close refusal family without naming in its own text what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be, and §3 names as new a CLI command that already exists in the 488-option surface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's closure-overview endpoint already exists as `reckon evidence synthesize`, and the figures section re-derives machinery that `reckon/crew/prompts.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py` and `reckon/crew/reports.py` already own.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2 adds a manifest check and §5 adds a page writer on top of mechanisms whose owners already exist; the plan states neither as an extension nor states any reason it cannot be.
